brief:
A genocide case brought by Gambia against Myanmar could establish new legal precedent with implications far beyond the Rohingya crisis, Middle East Eye reported. Judges in the International Court of Justice proceeding are preparing a ruling expected to influence how genocide law applies in other conflicts, including Israel's conduct in Gaza.

The case centers on Myanmar's military campaign against the Rohingya population, which began in September 2017. The court's interpretation of genocide statutes and the standards of proof required could set binding legal benchmarks for future cases before international tribunals.

title: Gambia's Myanmar case may reshape genocide law globally
